If you want to make a conference-style large-format poster using Quarto, this site has working templates for different style posters.

- The workflow uses Quarto and its `poster-typst` extension as a modern replacement for older `posterdown`/R Markdown poster workflows. 
- The workflow also uses Quarto's `_brand.yml` file to provide for consistent theming.
- Forking the repo allows you to access the templates and the supporting tools/scripts to check compliance.

::: callout-note
This is a student-oriented site, and it contains a lot of technical detail and rationale for why things are designed the way they are, from the templates to the theming to the testing and CI scripts.

- You do *not* need to understand all of the details to use the templates effectively -- see [Fork this repo and build your poster](#fork-this-repo-and-build-your-poster) to get going directly.
- The details matter for troubleshooting or customizing the templates, though, so they're here when you need them (Scripts & CI, Theming & Brand, Why Typst).
:::

> **Caveat:** Quarto's its `poster-typst` extension and `_brand.yml` theming are both still under active development. Several items in [Notes / gotchas](scripts-and-ci.qmd#notes-gotchas) describe current rough edges (local patches, path handling, caching) that a future Quarto/Typst release may resolve outright. If something documented here seems to have changed, check the current Quarto release notes before assuming the workaround is still needed.

> **AI Usage**: This project was developed with the assistance of Posit Assistant (Anthropic), which helped write and test code and text, most notably the theming, branding, and testing artifacts. The author has reviewed all elements and is responsible for any errors present at the time of publication; later software updates may introduce behavior the author has not reviewed.

 ## The Templates

There are three templates; each a single `.qmd` file that renders to **two** outputs:

| Format          | Purpose                | Engine |
|------------------------|--------------|--------|
| `poster-typst`  | Large-format print PDF (e.g. 36x24 in)     | [Typst](https://typst.app), via the `quarto-ext/typst-templates/poster` extension |
| `html`          | Responsive, scrollable "web poster" for posting online | Quarto HTML + custom SCSS |

- Because both formats are declared in one `format:` block, `quarto render poster.qmd` builds *both* versions from the same content in one pass.
    - Run `quarto render poster.qmd --to poster-typst` or `--to html` to build just one.
- The print PDF is typeset by **Typst**, not LaTeX. That choice drives several things in these templates (raw `` ```{=typst} `` blocks, arbitrary page sizes, no TeX install). 
    - See [Why Typst instead of LaTeX?](why-typst.qmd) for the reasoning and the trade-offs.
- `Rscript scripts/render-all.R` renders all three templates and then checks the output for known regressions. See [Scripts & CI](scripts-and-ci.qmd).

## Repo structure at a glance

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `templates/<name>/poster.qmd` | One self-contained poster. Start here. |
| `templates/<name>/*.scss` | That poster's web-only layout tweaks (loaded after the shared stylesheet below). |
| `scss/poster-common.scss` | Shared web "poster shell" styling used by all templates. |
| `_brand.yml` | Shared color palette + typography, consumed by Quarto's brand-aware HTML theming. See [Theming & Brand](theming.qmd#brand.yml-and-your-workflow). |
| `references.bib` | Shared bibliography (BibTeX), cited with `[@key]` from any template. |
| `images/` | Organization logo, plus generated preview images. |
| `scripts/` | R helpers: render everything, check output, audit contrast, regenerate previews. See [Scripts & CI](scripts-and-ci.qmd). |
| `_extensions/quarto-ext/poster/` | Vendored Typst poster extension, with three local patches. See [Notes / gotchas](scripts-and-ci.qmd#notes-gotchas). |
| `.github/workflows/posters.yml` | CI: renders every template and re-runs the checks on push/PR. |
| `docs-src/` | This site's source (a nested Quarto website project; renders to `docs/`). |
| `docs/` | The rendered, committed site GitHub Pages serves directly (Settings -> Pages: branch main, `/docs`). |

## Fork this repo and build your poster

Assuming you've forked or cloned this repo to build a poster of your own:

1. **Pick a starting template.** Skim the three options in [Templates](templates.qmd) and pick whichever layout fits your content. Each is a self-contained `templates/<name>/` folder that renders independently.
2. **Copy the folder**, e.g. `cp -r templates/01-classic-academic templates/my-poster`. Keep it under `templates/` so the shared registry in `scripts/templates.R`, and everything that reads it (`render-all.R`, `check-contrast.R`, `make-previews.R`), picks it up automatically. If your fork will only ever hold one poster, you can instead move that single `.qmd` (and its sibling `.scss`) to the project's top level and delete `templates/` entirely; the scripts auto-detect either layout (see [Scripts & CI](scripts-and-ci.qmd)).
3. **Edit the YAML front matter**: title, authors/affiliations, `poster-authors`, `departments`, footer contact info, and a print `size` (any Typst `"WIDTHxHEIGHT"` in inches. See [Choosing a print size](templates.qmd#choosing-a-print-size) for sizes that match common conference boards).
4. **Replace the `##` sections** with your own content. Each level-2 heading becomes a poster panel automatically, in both outputs. Cite sources with `[@bibkey]` and add the matching entry to `references.bib`.
5. **Re-color it if you're forking for a different organization.** The palette lives in a small, documented set of places. 
    - See [Re-coloring the templates](theming.qmd#re-coloring-the-templates)
    - `_brand.yml` drives the web theme specifically (see [Theming & Brand](theming.qmd#brand.yml-and-your-workflow)).
6. **Render it**: `quarto render templates/my-poster/poster.qmd`. Check `poster.pdf` for the printable version and `poster.html` for the web version.
7. **Run the checks** (optional, but worth it before you consider it done): `Rscript scripts/render-all.R` renders every template it finds and checks the output for known regressions. See [Scripts & CI](scripts-and-ci.qmd).
8. **Regenerate the previews** if you want updated images for your own README: `Rscript scripts/make-previews.R` (after re-rendering the PDFs).

## Requirements

**To render a poster itself:** [Quarto](https://quarto.org) (a version at or near the one pinned in [`.quarto-version`](https://github.com/AU-datascience/poster_templates/blob/main/.quarto-version)) and R since every template's R code chunks are part of the *shipped example content*, not the poster mechanism itself.

- When you replace the demo analysis with your own R or Python code, only your own code's package requirements apply. 

As shipped, the three example posters use:

- `tidyverse`, `palmerpenguins`, `patchwork` (all three templates)
- `broom` (`01-classic-academic` only, for `broom::tidy()` model summaries)
- `knitr` (all three, for `knitr::kable()` tables -- normally auto-loaded by Quarto's R engine, listed here for completeness)

No Python packages are required unless you add your own Python chunks. 

No system libraries beyond a working R + Quarto install are needed for the print or web render themselves.

- fonts (`Source Sans 3`, `STIX Two Text`) are fetched from Google and cached by Quarto at render time (see [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AU-datascience/poster_templates/blob/main/AGENTS.md)'s "Fonts" section), not installed as system fonts.

**To run the helper scripts in `scripts/`:** all four use `tidyverse` and `here`.

-  `make-previews.R` additionally needs `magick` (which needs the ImageMagick system library), and 
- `check-column-balance.R` needs `pdftools` (which needs the poppler system library). 
- `check-contrast.R` needs only `tidyverse`/`here` -- it's pure source/CSS parsing, no rendering. 

None of the scripts are required to render a poster; `quarto render templates/<name>/poster.qmd` alone is enough. 
- They exist to catch regressions (see [Scripts & CI](scripts-and-ci.qmd)), and CI (`.github/workflows/posters.yml`) installs all of the above automatically via `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies`, so you never need to install anything by hand just to see CI pass on a fork.

**Is this an `renv` repo?** No, deliberately not. 

- `renv` buys strict, pinned reproducibility of exact package versions, at the cost of a lockfile contributors must keep in sync and an `renv::restore()` step before anything runs. 
- For a small, stable package list on a repo meant to be forked and heavily edited by students building their own poster content (who will be adding whatever packages *their* analysis needs, not constrained by a lockfile), that friction outweighs the benefit here. 
- If you want tighter reproducibility *for your own fork*, e.g., pinning exact versions for a team where everyone must get identical output, `renv::init()` after cloning is a reasonable thing to layer on yourself; it just isn't part of this template.
